evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.3: ego locum aestāte umbrōsiōrem vīdī numquam
Hor. S. 2.8.3–4: ut mihi numquam in vītā fuerit melius
terms.comment: After “and”, Latin says nec umquam: mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse (Cic. Fam. 14.3.5). Numquam nōn is “always” (see always).

phrases.latin: ego locum aestāte umbrōsiōrem vīdī numquam
phrases.english: I have never seen a shadier spot in summer

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās et ita tibi persuādeās, mihi tē cārius nihil esse nec umquam fuisse
phrases.english: look after yourself, and be sure that nothing is or ever was dearer to me than you

sources: Lewis & Short: numquam · Lewis & Short: posthac
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 88.
